messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#595] keyval with constant value
parts:
try 
map = function(k,v) {x = rep(1, length(v)); keyval(x,x)}

R is vectorized and rmr follows that style by combination of choice and necessity. It is documented and illustrated in many examples. Using Java as a reference point will cause you lots of frustration.

Antonio


On Wed, Feb 27, 2013 at 7:34 AM, Arun Rajagopal <arungra...@gmail.com> wrote:
testDataSingle contains 55 lines on which each line is a random word. On running same equivalent code in java mapreduce what we get is the set of keys and values such that keys is no.of lines in the file times '1' and values as  no.of lines in the file times '1'. It means that the map function runs for no.of lines time. But when I use rmr2, I get keys as 1,1 values as 1,1. I checked the cluster statistics where I came to know is that the whole input file is split into two part and the map function runs for only once in each part, yielding only two values. Please enlighten me on this issue.


CODE: out2 = mapreduce(input="/user/hadoop/testDataSingle.txt",map = function(k,v) keyval(1, 1),reduce = NULL)
output2<-from.dfs(out2)


P.S: when I use non constant values inside keyval, it works fine.
